from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Prerequisite Review: The Two Faces of a Curve"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's explore the two faces of a curve.",
            "Differentiation measures the steepness at a point.",
            "Integration calculates the total area underneath."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        BLUE_COLOR = "#58C4DD"
        RED_COLOR = "#F91717"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#87C2A5"

        # Setup Coordinate System
        # Occupies area from B1 to F6
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        x_label = Text("t", font_size=18).next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        y_label = Text("v(t)", font_size=18).next_to(axes.y_axis, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR))
        
        # Draw a horizontal blue line representing constant velocity
        # v(t) = 2
        velocity_line = axes.plot(lambda t: 2, x_range=[0, 5], color=BLUE_COLOR)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(Create(velocity_line), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED_COLOR))
        
        # Add red arrow pointing to the line with text "Slope = 0 (Acceleration)"
        slope_point = axes.c2p(2, 2)
        slope_arrow = Arrow(
            start=slope_point + UP * 1.5 + LEFT * 0.5, 
            end=slope_point, 
            color=RED_COLOR,
            buff=0.1
        )
        slope_label = Text("Slope = 0\n(Acceleration)", font_size=18, color=RED_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        # Adjust label to be near arrow
        slope_label.next_to(slope_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(slope_arrow), Write(slope_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN_COLOR))
        
        # Gradually fill area from t=0 to t=4 under the line
        area = axes.get_area(velocity_line, x_range=[0, 4], color=GREEN_COLOR, opacity=0.4)
        area_label = Text("Area (Distance)", font_size=20, color=GREEN_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(area, shift=UP), run_time=2)
        self.play(Write(area_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'The derivative captures change at a single moment.',
            'Zooming in, any curve looks like a line.',
            'This straight line represents the instantaneous slope.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Derivative: Capturing the Momentary Change", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        BLUE_CURVE = "#58C4DD"
        YELLOW_DOT = "#FFFF00"
        RED_TANGENT = "#F91717"
        WHITE_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # Initialize Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 5, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "stroke_width": 2},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Labels for axes
        x_label = Text("t (sec)", font_size=16).next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        y_label = Text("s(t) (pos)", font_size=16).next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        
        # The Curve: s(t) = 0.25 * t^2 (Rabbit Swift's position)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda t: 0.25 * t**2, x_range=[0, 4.2], color=BLUE_CURVE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_CURVE)
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(Create(curve), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Step 2: Yellow dot at t=2
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_DOT)
        
        dot_pos = axes.c2p(2, 1) # s(2) = 0.25 * 4 = 1
        moment_dot = Dot(point=dot_pos, color=YELLOW_DOT, radius=0.08)
        dot_label = Text("t=2", font_size=20, color=YELLOW_DOT).next_to(moment_dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(moment_dot), Write(dot_label))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 3: Zooming in
        # Group everything to scale around the dot
        zoom_group = VGroup(axes, curve, moment_dot, dot_label, x_label, y_label)
        
        # Perform the zoom effect centered on the dot
        self.play(
            zoom_group.animate.scale(4, about_point=dot_pos),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED_TANGENT)

        # Step 4: Overlay a red tangent line
        # Tangent for y = 0.25x^2 at x=2 has slope y' = 0.5x = 1.
        # Tangent equation: y - 1 = 1(x - 2) -> y = x - 1
        tangent_line = axes.plot(lambda t: t - 1, x_range=[1.2, 2.8], color=RED_TANGENT)
        # Note: Since the axes were scaled, the tangent plot using axes.plot will scale correctly relative to the dot
        
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        
        # Step 5: Display text 's'(2): Instantaneous Speed'
        # We place this near the tangent line using grid coordinates or relative to the zoomed group
        speed_text = Text("s'(2): Instantaneous Speed", font_size=24, color=WHITE_TEXT)
        self.place_at_grid(speed_text, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(speed_text))
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset lecture colors to white for end of section
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Integral: The Art of Accumulation"
        lecture_lines = [
            'Integration is the art of accumulating tiny parts.',
            'We sum infinite rectangles to find total area.',
            'Gaps vanish as rectangles become infinitely thin.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define the function for the "rate of rainfall"
        def rainfall_rate(x):
            return 1.5 + 0.6 * np.sin(x) + 0.4 * np.cos(2 * x)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Step 1: Draw a blue wavy curve (#58C4DD)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#58C4DD")
        
        # Create Axes for the graph
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_range=[0, 3, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": WHITE},
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        curve = axes.plot(rainfall_rate, x_range=[0, 6], color="#58C4DD")
        curve_label = Text("Rate of Rainfall", font_size=16, color="#58C4DD")
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, 'A4', scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(curve_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Step 2: Create 6 thick green rectangles (#87C2A5) under the curve
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#87C2A5")
        
        num_rects = ValueTracker(6)
        
        # Get Riemann Rectangles (Left sum for clarity)
        rects = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve, 
            x_range=[0, 6], 
            dx=6 / int(num_rects.get_value()), 
            stroke_width=1, 
            fill_opacity=0.6, 
            color="#87C2A5",
            input_sample_type="left"
        ))
        
        self.play(Create(rects), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Step 3: Increase the number of rectangles to 100
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#87C2A5")
        
        # Transition from 6 to 100 rectangles
        self.play(
            num_rects.animate.set_value(100),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivatives and integrals are actually inverse operations.",
            "Integration finds total area from a rate.",
            "Differentiation finds the rate from total area.",
            "They reverse each other like addition and subtraction.",
            "This is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Connection: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_DIFF = "#F91717" # Red
        COLOR_INT = "#58C4DD"  # Blue
        COLOR_MACHINE = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Step 1: Create a white box labeled 'The Magic Machine'
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        machine_rect = Rectangle(width=3.5, height=2.0, color=COLOR_MACHINE)
        machine_text = Text("The Magic Machine", font_size=20, color=COLOR_MACHINE)
        machine_text.shift(UP * 0.7) # Slight internal shift
        machine_group = VGroup(machine_rect, machine_text)
        
        self.place_in_area(machine_group, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(machine_rect), Write(machine_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Step 2: Animate symbol F(x) moving into the left side of the box
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid system dependency on 'latex' executable
        f_cap_x = Text("F(x)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(f_cap_x, 'B1', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(f_cap_x))
        # Move F(x) to the center of the machine
        machine_center = self.grid['B3'] + DOWN * 0.2
        self.play(f_cap_x.animate.move_to(machine_center))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Step 3: Inside the box, flash a red d/dx operator
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIFF))
        
        diff_op = Text("d/dx", color=COLOR_DIFF)
        self.place_at_grid(diff_op, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Flash(diff_op, color=COLOR_DIFF, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(FadeIn(diff_op))
        
        # Transform F(x) to f(x) to represent differentiation
        f_small_x = Text("f(x)", color=WHITE)
        f_small_x.move_to(f_cap_x.get_center())
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(f_cap_x, f_small_x),
            FadeOut(diff_op, shift=DOWN*0.2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Step 4: Animate symbol f(x) moving out of the right side of the box
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        exit_pos = self.grid['B6']
        self.play(f_small_x.animate.move_to(exit_pos))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Step 5: Show f(x) entering an integral chamber returning to F(x) + C
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_INT))
        
        # Create Integral Chamber
        int_box = Rectangle(width=3.0, height=1.5, color=COLOR_INT)
        int_symbol = Text("∫", color=COLOR_INT, font_size=50)
        int_chamber = VGroup(int_box, int_symbol)
        self.place_in_area(int_chamber, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(int_box), Write(int_symbol))
        
        # Move f(x) into chamber
        chamber_center = self.grid['E3'] + RIGHT * 0.5
        self.play(f_small_x.animate.move_to(chamber_center))
        
        # Final result F(x) + C
        result_tex = Text("F(x) + C", color=COLOR_INT)
        result_tex.move_to(chamber_center)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(f_small_x, result_tex))
        self.play(Indicate(result_tex, color=COLOR_INT))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Step-by-Step Visualization: The Growing Area"
        lines = [
            "Watch the area grow as we move x.",
            "A tiny shift adds a thin sliver.",
            "The height of this sliver is f(x).",
            "The growth rate is exactly the curve's height.",
            "So, the derivative of area equals the function."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Helper for coordinates
        # Axes will be placed in the B2-F6 area
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        def func(x):
            return 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5
        
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color="#58C4DD")
        
        # Initial area A(x)
        x_val = 2.0
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_val], color="#87C2A5", opacity=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#87C2A5"))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        dx = 0.4
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Using line_func=DashedLine as supported by CE axes.get_vertical_line
        line_x = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.c2p(x_val, func(x_val)), color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        line_xdx = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.c2p(x_val + dx, func(x_val + dx)), color=WHITE, line_func=DashedLine)
        
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency errors
        label_x = Text("x", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(line_x, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_xdx = Text("x+dx", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(line_xdx, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(line_x), Create(line_xdx), Write(label_x), Write(label_xdx))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Yellow strip (the sliver)

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Practical Application: The Cheetah's Sprint", 
            [
                "A cheetah's sprint demonstrates calculus in action.",
                "Integrating acceleration twice reveals the total distance.",
                "Calculus reconstructs the journey from movement data."
            ]
        )
        
        # Color definitions
        ACCEL_COLOR = "#F91717"
        VELOC_COLOR = "#58C4DD"
        DIST_COLOR = WHITE

        # Function definitions for the sprint
        def a_func(t): return 3 * np.exp(-0.8 * t)
        def v_func(t): return (3 / 0.8) * (1 - np.exp(-0.8 * t))
        def s_func(t): return (3 / 0.8) * (t + (1 / 0.8) * np.exp(-0.8 * t) - (1 / 0.8))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ACCEL_COLOR)
        
        # Create axes for a(t) and v(t)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Fixed: Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX requirement
        labels = axes.get_axis_labels(
            x_label=Text("t", font_size=24), 
            y_label=Text("y", font_size=24)
        )
        a_graph = axes.plot(a_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=ACCEL_COLOR)
        a_label = Text("a(t)", color=ACCEL_COLOR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(a_label, "B5")

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(labels))
        self.play(Create(a_graph), Write(a_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(VELOC_COLOR)
        
        # Area under acceleration graph
        area = axes.get_area(a_graph, x_range=[0, 4], color=VELOC_COLOR, opacity=0.3)
        v_graph = axes.plot(v_func, x_range=[0, 4], color=VELOC_COLOR)
        v_label = Text("v(t)", color=VELOC_COLOR, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "C5")

        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.play(Create(v_graph), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(DIST_COLOR)
        
        # Create a track for the cheetah
        track_line = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color=GRAY_D)
        track_group = VGroup(track_line)
        self.place_in_area(track_group, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        cheetah_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        cheetah_dot.move_to(track_line.get_start())
        
        dist_text = Text("Distance:", font_size=20).next_to(track_line, UP, buff=0.2)
        # Fixed: Added mob_class=Text to DecimalNumber to avoid 'latex' dependency
        dist_value = DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places=2, font_size=20, mob_class=Text).next_to(dist_text, RIGHT)
        dist_group = VGroup(dist_text, dist_value)
        
        self.play(Create(track_line), FadeIn(cheetah_dot), Write(dist_group))
        
        # Use ValueTracker to animate distance calculation
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Add updaters
        cheetah_dot.add_updater(
            lambda m: m.move_to(
                track_line.point_from_proportion(s_func(time_tracker.get_value()) / s_func(4))
            )
        )
        dist_value.add_updater(
            lambda m: m.set_value(s_func(time_tracker.get_value()))
        )
        
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Cleanup updaters
        cheetah_dot.clear_updaters()
        dist_value.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Bridge Between Change and Accumulation: The Relationship Between Derivatives and Integrals
outline.target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university students

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Faces of a Curve
sections.content: Briefly revisit the concepts of 'Slope' and 'Area' using a simple linear graph. Establish the visual foundation: differentiation looks at the steepness at a point, while integration looks at the space under the line.
sections.example: Visual: A straight-line graph representing a car's constant speed. Show the slope (acceleration) is 0, while the area under the line (distance) is a growing rectangle.

sections.title: The Derivative: Capturing the Momentary Change
sections.content: Define the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change. Use the 'Zoom-in' animation technique to show that any curve, when magnified enough, looks like a straight line (the tangent).
sections.example: Character: A rabbit named 'Swift'. If Swift's position is $s(t)$, the derivative $s'(t)$ is his speedometer reading at exactly $t=2$ seconds.

sections.title: The Integral: The Art of Accumulation
sections.content: Introduce the definite integral as the 'sum of infinite tiny parts'. Visualize the area under a curve being filled by increasingly thin rectangles (Riemann Sums) until the gaps disappear.
sections.example: Visual: A rain gauge filling up during a storm. The 'rate of rainfall' is the curve; the 'total water collected' is the integral (the area accumulated over time).

sections.title: The Core Connection: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
sections.content: Explain that differentiation and integration are inverse operations, much like addition and subtraction. If you integrate a function to find the area $A(x)$, then the rate at which that area grows ($A'(x)$) is exactly the original function $f(x)$.
sections.example: Animation: A 'Magic Machine'. Put a position function in, differentiate to get velocity; put that velocity back into the 'Integration Chamber' to regain the original position function (plus a constant $C$).

sections.title: Step-by-Step Visualization: The Growing Area
sections.content: Demonstrate why the derivative of the area function is the original curve. Show a moving vertical boundary $x$. As $x$ moves by a tiny bit $dx$, the area increases by a thin sliver of height $f(x)$ and width $dx$.
sections.example: Graphical representation: A shaded region under $y = x^2$. As we nudge the boundary from $x$ to $x + dx$, the new area added is roughly a rectangle of height $x^2$. Therefore, $dA/dx = x^2$.

sections.title: Practical Application: The Cheetah's Sprint
sections.content: Apply the concept to a real-world physics scenario. If we have the acceleration data of a cheetah, we can reconstruct its entire journey.
sections.example: Device: A Cheetah-mounted GPS. The device records acceleration (derivative of velocity). By integrating twice, we can animate the Cheetah's path on a map and calculate exactly how far it traveled to catch its prey.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap the 'Inverse Relationship'. Emphasize that the integral provides the 'Total Result' of a changing process, while the derivative provides the 'Rate' of that process.
sections.example: Visual: A 'Loop' icon showing: Position $\xrightarrow{d/dx}$ Velocity $\xrightarrow{d/dx}$ Acceleration, and Acceleration $\xrightarrow{\int}$ Velocity $\xrightarrow{\int}$ Position.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Faces of a Curve
lecture_lines: Consider a car moving at a constant velocity.
The flat slope means acceleration is exactly zero.
The shaded area represents the total distance traveled.
animations: Step 1: Draw a horizontal blue line (#58C4DD) representing constant velocity v(t) on a 2D plane.
Step 2: Add a red arrow (#F91717) pointing to the line with the text 'Slope = 0 (Acceleration)'.
Step 3: Gradually fill the rectangular region from t=0 to t=4 under the line with green (#87C2A5) to show 'Area (Distance)'.

storyboard.title: The Derivative: Capturing the Momentary Change
lecture_lines: Swift's position changes over time along this curve.
Let's focus on his movement at two seconds.
Zooming in, the curve eventually looks perfectly straight.
This tangent line reveals the slope at that moment.
It represents Swift's instantaneous speed at that point.
animations: Step 1: Draw a blue curve (#58C4DD) representing rabbit Swift's position s(t) on a 2D plane.
Step 2: Place a yellow dot (#FFFF00) at t=2 on the curve to mark a specific moment.
Step 3: Scale up the camera view centered at the dot until the curve segment appears as a straight line.
Step 4: Overlay a red tangent line (#F91717) passing through the yellow dot to show the slope.
Step 5: Display the text 's\u2032(2): Instantaneous Speed' in white (#FFFFFF) next to the tangent.

storyboard.title: The Integral: The Art of Accumulation
lecture_lines: A wavy curve tracks the changing rate of rainfall.
We approximate total water using a few thick rectangles.
Infinite thin rectangles fill the area perfectly.
animations: Step 1: Draw a blue wavy curve (#58C4DD) representing the fluctuating rate of rainfall over time.
Step 2: Create 6 thick green rectangles (#87C2A5) under the curve to approximate the total water collected.
Step 3: Increase the number of rectangles to 100, showing them becoming thinner and perfectly filling the area.

storyboard.title: The Core Connection: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
lecture_lines: Calculus uses a "Magic Machine" to connect functions.
First, we feed a position function into the machine.
The differentiation operator calculates the rate of change.
Out comes the velocity function, describing the motion.
Integrating this velocity returns us to the original position.
animations: Step 1: Create a white box (#FFFFFF) in the center labeled 'The Magic Machine'.
Step 2: Animate a symbol F(x) moving into the left side of the box.
Step 3: Inside the box, flash a red d/dx operator (#F91717) to represent differentiation.
Step 4: Animate a symbol f(x) moving out of the right side of the box.
Step 5: Show f(x) entering an integral chamber \u222b in blue (#58C4DD) to return to F(x) + C.

storyboard.title: Step-by-Step Visualization: The Growing Area
lecture_lines: Let the green area represent the accumulated total.
Nudge the boundary forward by a tiny amount, dx.
This creates a thin sliver of new area.
The sliver’s height is determined by the curve’s value.
Thus, the rate of area growth is the function.
animations: Step 1: Plot a blue curve y=f(x) (#58C4DD) and shade the area A(x) under it in green (#87C2A5).
Step 2: Draw a vertical dashed line at position x and another at x + dx.
Step 3: Fill the thin vertical strip between x and x + dx with yellow (#FFFF00) to show area growth.
Step 4: Add labels f(x) for the height and dx for the width of the yellow strip in white (#FFFFFF).

Step 5: Display the formula dA = f(x) \u00b7 dx, concluding that dA/dx = f(x), and place the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/based.svg] icon next to the final result to signify its importance.

storyboard.title: Practical Application: The Cheetah's Sprint
lecture_lines: We start with the cheetah’s recorded acceleration data.
Integrating acceleration gives the cheetah’s changing velocity.
A second integration calculates the total distance covered.
animations: Step 1: Draw a red acceleration curve a(t) (#F91717) representing a cheetah's sprint.
Step 2: Shade the area under the curve to transform it into a blue velocity graph v(t) (#58C4DD).
Step 3: Animate a small dot moving along a path to represent the cheetah's accumulated distance.

storyboard.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are two sides of one coin.
They function as inverse operations, reversing each other.
Together, they link momentary change to total accumulation.
animations: Step 1: Display the words 'Differentiation' and 'Integration' at opposite sides of the screen in white (#FFFFFF).
Step 2: Draw a circular orange arrow (#FC6255) connecting the two terms to show they are inverses.
Step 3: Display the sequences s \u2192 v \u2192 a and a \u2192 v \u2192 s in blue (#58C4DD) to summarize the loop.

issues.description: [section_6] Implement Manim code for the cheetah application. Apply derivative and integral concepts to acceleration and distance. Sync 3 steps with 3 lecture lines.
issues.resolution_note: Implemented the cheetah sprint scenario with three distinct steps: 1) Acceleration curve a(t) in red, 2) Integral/Area under curve transforming to velocity v(t) in blue, 3) Real-world path/distance animation using a moving dot. Linked animations to the three lecture lines.

issues.description: [section_7] Implement Manim code for the summary and conclusion. Summarize the inverse relationship and the calculus loop. Sync 3 steps with 3 lecture lines.
issues.resolution_note: Created 3-step animation: 1) Differentiation/Integration text, 2) Orange loop arrows, 3) Physics sequences (s->v->a), synced with lecture lines.
